Team + partners —

We need to tighten the ETA window for the Nimbus dedicated pool so we can finalize the deal economics and onboarding SOW. Current ask: Nimbus expects a production-ready dedicated pool to begin serving traffic by Nov 15, 2026. That leaves a compressed hardware onramp and potential need for a cloud fallback for the first 8 weeks.

What I need from each of you by EOD Wed (26 Aug):
- OEM (Lena): consolidated, line-itemed lead times for the requested SKUs (A100 80GB, H100 80GB family) with earliest partial-shipment dates, expedite options and incremental cost for split shipments. Attach a marked-up quote we can attach to the SOW.
- Cloud (Todd): confirmation of available reserved capacity or short-term burst pools in us-west-2 and us-east-1, plus minimum commitment terms and any fast-availability windows we can contract against. Link to booking if possible.
- Internal (Vanessa / Karthik / Ben): a proposed staging plan (tranche sizes + ramp weeks) and a commercial fallback proposal if we need to use cloud capacity while hardware ships.

Attached: Nimbus_OEM_quote_comparison_v1.xlsx — my attempt to reconcile the two OEM quotes we received earlier. I'm purposely including Sam so Nimbus can weigh in on acceptable partial-capacity thresholds (e.g., % of steady-state tokens) and any regulatory constraints.

Thanks —
Rohan

Hi Rohan / Sam / Vanessa —

Thanks for the clear ask. Attached is an updated quote (OGEMO_Nimbus_quote_v3.pdf) that reflects current manufacturing slot availability for the A100/H100 families. Key points: 
- Standard lead time for A100 80GB: 14–18 weeks from PO receipt. H100 80GB: 20–26 weeks, current queueing driven by wafer allocation.
- We can do a partial shipment (50% of units) ~12 weeks after PO, with balance shipped on a two-week cadence thereafter. Partial shipments carry a 6% expedite fee per partial shipment.
- We can prioritize up to one tranche per month if you place a non-refundable slot deposit (suggested 10% deposit) to secure the slot.
- Customs/transport typical add-on (estimated): 5–8 business days depending on FCA/EXW terms.

If Redwood needs a firmer commitment we can add a shipment penalty clause, but that requires a longer lead-time guarantee window on your side (we'd want a signed MSA + purchase schedule).

Attached: OGEMO_Nimbus_quote_v3.pdf

Rohan / all —

Short answer: we have immediate reserve capacity options that can cover initial traffic while hardware ships. Summary below: 
- us-west-2: Reserved Compute Pool (RC-P) — available immediately with 2-week activation; supports NVidia H100 equivalence via accelerated instances. Minimum 4-week commitment, prorated daily.
- us-east-1: Spot-accelerated short bursts available but capacity less guaranteed; recommended only as overflow.
- Fast-reserve add-on: for deals like Nimbus we can hold a pre-warmed lane for up to 8 weeks with a refundable deposit; we'd need an LOI to lock the lane.

Link to reserve booking: https://portal.cloudco.com/reservations/rcp-4287

We can provide a written guarantee for the RC-P activation timeline in your SOW but we cannot guarantee OEM-equivalent latencies without Redwood-side runtime tuning (batching/quantization) — something to factor into the SLO conversation.

Happy to jump on a short call to outline costs (per-hour + 4-week minimum).

—Todd

Thanks — quick operational take below.

Proposed staging plan (rough):
- Week 0–4 (Nov 15 target): CloudCo RC-P to cover 40% of steady-state token capacity.
- Week 5–8: First OEM partial shipment -> onboard 50% of requested GPU count; combined with RC-P to hit ~85% capacity.
- Week 9–12: Remaining OEM shipments; full capacity reached by week 12.

Sizing assumptions: steady-state need = 200 x 80GB-equivalent GPUs (peak token throughput). Tranche sizes = 100 (partial), 100 (balance).

Requests / open questions:
- Ben: commercial fallback terms (credits, price premium) we can offer if CloudCo is used beyond 8 weeks.
- Vanessa: confirm feasibility of staggered onboarding windows and whether we can accept split PO for OEM (for customs/invoicing).

I've attached a quick capacity_model_rough.csv (very rough) showing throughput curves under the hybrid plan. We should align with Nimbus on what "acceptable" % of capacity in first 6 weeks is.

-Karthik
